# Log Upgrades and Repairs in the Activity Trail

Ensure that every time a hardware upgrade or repair is created, updated, or imported from a CSV, a corresponding record is created in the Activity Trail (Transaction History) table.

## Proposed Changes

---

### Core Application Logic

#### [MODIFY] [app.js](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/app.js)

- **`changeMaintStatus`**: Add a call to `logTransaction` whenever a maintenance log's status is modified (e.g., from `In Progress` or `Awaiting Parts` to `Completed`), so that these status transitions are visible in the activity trail.
- **`importMaintenanceFromCSV`**: Update the CSV parsing loop to generate individual transaction log entries of type `'Maintenance'` for each imported log record. Prepend these transactions in bulk to `state.transactions` before saving the state, preventing performance issues from repeated individual writes.

---

### Demo Data Seeding

#### [MODIFY] [demo-data.js](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/demo-data.js)

- **`DEFAULT_TRANSACTIONS`**: Add a missing default transaction for the third maintenance record (`m-03` on the HP ProBook 450 G10) so that all initial repair logs are correctly represented in the activity trail on first startup/data seeding.

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Open the application.
2. Under Settings, click **Seed Demo Data** (or reset and seed) and check if all three demo maintenance entries show up under the **Activity Trail** tab when filtering by **Maintenance** or **All Actions**.

# Replace Warranty & Alerts with Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs on Dashboard

The user requested that instead of seeing the "Warranty & Alerts" card on the dashboard, they want to see the "Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs" ordered by date (newest first).

## Proposed Changes

---

### Dashboard Markup

#### [MODIFY] [index.html](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/index.html)

- Replace the `<!-- Warranty & Alerts -->` card element structure with a new `<!-- Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs -->` structure:
  - Update card title header text.
  - Replace the container ID `#alerts-container` with `#dashboard-maint-container`.
  - Update the empty state icon/text to reflect maintenance logs instead of warranty warnings.

---

### Core Application Logic

#### [MODIFY] [app.js](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/app.js)

- **`DOM` References**: Update `DOM.alertsContainer` reference to `DOM.dashboardMaintContainer` targeting the `#dashboard-maint-container` element.
- **`renderDashboardAlerts` (Rename & Refactor)**:
  - Rename `renderDashboardAlerts()` to `renderDashboardMaintenanceLogs()`.
  - Inside the function, retrieve `state.maintenance`, sort logs by date in descending order (newest first), and render each log as a clickable list item.
  - Each list item will display the asset name/tag, replacement part, status (with styled badges), description, and performed date.
  - Bind a click listener on each log item to open the details drawer of the respective asset.
- **`renderAll`**: Update the call from `renderDashboardAlerts()` to `renderDashboardMaintenanceLogs()`.

---

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Open the application.
2. Verify that on the **Dashboard** page:
   - The card title is now **Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs**.
   - It lists all pre-seeded and manually added maintenance logs sorted from newest to oldest date.
3. Click on any log item in the dashboard card; it should successfully open the slide-out details drawer for that asset.
4. Try adding a new upgrade/repair through the inventory grid (using the inspections drawer). Verify that it immediately appears at the top of the dashboard maintenance logs card.

args.CodeContent:
# Add Pagination to Dashboard Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs

The user requested that "per page five most hardware upgrade and replacement logs should be shown." This means we should add interactive pagination controls to the Dashboard card to allow paginated viewing (5 items per page) of all logs.

## Proposed Changes

---

### Dashboard Markup

#### [MODIFY] [index.html](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/index.html)

- Under `#dashboard-maint-container`, add a pagination controls container (`#dashboard-maint-pagination`) featuring:
  - Page information text indicator (`#dashboard-maint-info`).
  - Interactive previous (`#btn-dash-maint-prev`) and next (`#btn-dash-maint-next`) navigation buttons.

---

### Core Application Logic

#### [MODIFY] [app.js](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/app.js)

- **`dashboardMaintPagination` config**: Define a global pagination state containing `currentPage: 1` and `pageSize: 5`.
- **`DOM` References**: Bind the new HTML pagination elements (`#dashboard-maint-pagination`, `#dashboard-maint-info`, `#btn-dash-maint-prev`, and `#btn-dash-maint-next`).
- **`setupEventListeners`**: Register click listeners for the prev/next buttons to change pages and re-render the list.
- **`renderDashboardMaintenanceLogs`**:
  - Implement dynamic page slicing of date-sorted maintenance logs (5 items per page based on `dashboardMaintPagination.currentPage`).
  - Render page logs in the container.
  - Dynamically display/hide the pagination panel depending on whether the total log count exceeds 5.
  - Set active/disabled states for the pagination controls.
- **Form Submits & CSV Imports**: Reset `dashboardMaintPagination.currentPage = 1` on new logs additions or imports.

---

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Open the application.
2. Verify that on the **Dashboard** page:
   - If there are 5 or fewer logs, the pagination controls are hidden.
   - If there are more than 5 logs, pagination controls appear at the bottom of the card displaying `Page 1 of X` with `Prev` disabled and `Next` enabled.
3. Click `Next` to navigate to page 2, check that the next 5 logs are displayed, and that the page indicator updates.
4. Verify that clicking `Prev` brings you back to page 1.
5. Click a log on page 2 and confirm that it still opens the correct asset drawer.
6. Verify that adding a new maintenance log resets the view back to Page 1, showing the newly logged upgrade at the top.

# Add Total Monthly Costing for Upgrades and Repairs on Dashboard

The user requested to see the total costing per month on hardware upgrades & replacements directly on the dashboard. We will implement a toggle tab at the top of the **Hardware Upgrade & Replacement** card to switch between the detailed logs timeline view and a monthly costing breakdown view.

## Proposed Changes

---

### Dashboard Markup

#### [MODIFY] [index.html](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/index.html)

- **Card Header**: Add tab buttons (`#btn-maint-tab-logs` and `#btn-maint-tab-cost`) to the title bar of the **Hardware Upgrade & Replacement Logs** card.
- **Card Body**:
  - Keep `#dashboard-maint-container` for rendering detailed logs.
  - Add a new container `#dashboard-maint-cost-container` (hidden by default) for rendering the monthly cost breakdown list.

---

### Core Application Logic

#### [MODIFY] [app.js](file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/app.js)

- **Global Config**: Define a global state variable `activeMaintTab = 'logs'` to track the active view tab.
- **DOM References**: Bind the new tab buttons and container element mappings.
- **setupEventListeners**: Bind click listeners to handle switching between the logs tab and monthly costing tab.
- **`switchMaintTab(tab)`**: Create a function to toggle tab button styling, show/hide the appropriate list containers, toggle the logs page navigation controls, and trigger the correct render function.
- **`renderDashboardMonthlyCost()`**:
  - Create this function to aggregate cost from `state.maintenance` logs by month (e.g., "June 2026", "May 2025").
  - Order the months chronologically descending (newest first).
  - Calculate and display a premium centered **Total Hardware Costing** grand summary block.
  - Render each month's total cost in an elegant list format.
- **`renderAll()`**: Conditionally call `renderDashboardMaintenanceLogs()` or `renderDashboardMonthlyCost()` based on `activeMaintTab`.

---

## Verification Plan

### Manual Verification
1. Open the application and navigate to the **Dashboard** page.
2. Confirm the **Hardware Upgrade & Replacement** card now has **Logs** and **Monthly Cost** tab buttons in the header.
3. Click the **Monthly Cost** button and verify that:
   - The card switches to display a centered grand total cost (e.g., sum of all repairs).
   - Below the grand total, it lists aggregated monthly costs (e.g., `June 2026: $110.00`, `May 2025: $135.00`, `February 2025: $65.00`) sorted with newest months first.
   - The pagination prev/next controls at the bottom of the card are hidden when this tab is active.
4. Click the **Logs** button and verify the card switches back to the detailed timeline logs list with page controls visible.
5. Go to the **Inventory Grid**, inspect an asset, and log a new upgrade with a cost of `$200.00` on a specific date (e.g., a new month). Switch to the **Monthly Cost** tab on the dashboard and verify that the month's total and the grand total are updated instantly.

## 🔒 Completed Maintenance Log Restrictions & Editing Capability

To enforce data integrity while allowing necessary adjustments to finalized maintenance work:
* **Edit Controls for Ongoing Work**: Added an "✏️ Edit" button inside the details drawer for ongoing (In Progress/Awaiting Parts/Unpaid) maintenance logs. This allows administrators to adjust parts description, vendor, cost, date, status, and reason.
* **One-Time Edit Allowance for Completed Logs**:
  - Replaced the absolute lock with a one-time edit policy: Completed maintenance logs display a `Completed (Can be edited 1 time)` indicator and an `✏️ Edit` button.
  - Once the log is edited and submitted (or its status shifted via the toggles), the edit count increases to `1`, which hides the `✏️ Edit` button from the drawer view.
  - Added strict programmatic guards in `changeMaintStatus` and `handleMaintenanceSubmit` to verify that no log that has already been edited once after completion can be modified again. Trying to do so triggers the alert: `This completed record has already been edited once and cannot be modified again.`

---

## 💸 Maintenance Status Update - Unpaid Option

To support tracking repair expenses before final payment/invoice settlement:
* **Status Dropdown**: Added an `Unpaid` option to the Maintenance Status select input in the log entry modal (positioned logically before `Completed`).
* **UI styling**: Created a premium Indigo style badge (`.maint-unpaid`) to represent this state.
* **Transition Controls**: The drawer's status toggles now support transitioning to and from `Unpaid` alongside `In Progress` and `Awaiting Parts`.
* **Workflow Integrity**: While a log has an `Unpaid` status, the target asset correctly remains in the `Maintenance` status block. Only upon transition to `Completed` is the asset released.

To transfer your complete IT asset inventory to another laptop with all data, images, passwords, and logs intact, you can use one of two methods. 

We highly recommend **Method 1 (Cloud Sync Token)** because it migrates your entire database (including attachments, user credentials, and history logs) instantly in a single step.

---

### Method 1: Connect via Cloud Sync Token (Recommended) ⚡
This method uses the built-in global synchronization feature to securely sync all data to the new laptop.

**On your current laptop:**
1. Open the application and go to the **Settings** tab.
2. Under the **Cloud Database Auto-Sync** panel, check if you already have a token connected.
   - If not, click **Generate Sync Token** (it will request an email for recovery).
   - Once connected, your status badge at the top will glow green and read `CLOUD CONNECTED`.
3. Click the **📋 Copy** button next to your **Cloud Sync Token** (a unique code like `4tU6Ryp2x2aP91mYtTfKzn`). Send this token to yourself (via email or chat) so you can access it on the new laptop.

**On the new laptop:**
1. Open the application files (or browse to the hosted URL).
2. On the **Login Screen**, click the link that says **Connect via Cloud Sync Token** (located below the password entry field).
3. Paste the **Sync Token** you copied from the old laptop and click **Connect & Load Database**.
4. You will receive a success popup. The entire database is now imported, and you can log in immediately using your administrative password!

---

### Method 2: Manual CSV Export & Import 📂
If you prefer a local offline transfer, you can export and import individual files.

**On your current laptop:**
1. Go to the **Inventory Grid** tab and click **Export CSV**.
2. Go to the **Vendors** tab and click **Export CSV**.
3. Go to the **Settings** tab, scroll down to the CSV Engine, and click **Export Maintenance CSV**.
4. Transfer these three `.csv` files to the new laptop (using a USB drive, email, or cloud sharing).

**On the new laptop:**
1. Open the application and log in as `admin`.
2. Go to the **Settings** tab.
3. Import the files using the corresponding buttons in the settings console:
   - Click **Import CSV** inside the Inventory Grid to load assets.
   - Click **Import CSV** inside the Vendors tab to load suppliers.
   - Click **Import Maintenance CSV** in Settings to load repair and parts replacement logs.

*Note: The CSV method does not migrate custom branding logos or base64 file attachments (like scanned receipts/photos) due to spreadsheet size limits. Use **Method 1** if you want files and custom passwords transferred.*

The application stores your inventory data inside the browser's **Local Storage** (`localStorage`). 

Because Local Storage is securely isolated by the browser based on the address (called the **Origin**), your data might appear "missing" if you opened the application differently this time. Here are the two most likely reasons and how to get your data back:

---

### Reason 1: You previously opened the app as a local file (`file:///`)
If you previously opened the application by double-clicking the `index.html` file directly, your browser saved the data under the `file://` address. Since `http://localhost:3000` is a different address, the browser starts with a fresh empty database.

**How to recover your data:**
1. Open your browser and navigate to the local file URL:
   `file:///C:/Users/ABIR/.gemini/antigravity/scratch/stock-inventory-app/index.html`
   *(Or simply double-click the `index.html` file in your file explorer).*
2. Verify that your entered data is visible there.
3. To move it to the local server:
   - **Using Cloud Sync**: Go to the **Settings** tab, generate a **Cloud Sync Token**, and copy it. Then, open `http://localhost:3000` in your browser, click **Connect via Cloud Sync Token** on the login screen, and paste the token to sync everything.
   - **Using CSV**: Go to the **Inventory Grid** / **Settings** tab, click **Export CSV** for your assets and maintenance logs, then open `http://localhost:3000` and click the corresponding **Import CSV** buttons.

---

### Reason 2: You previously used a different web browser
Local Storage is unique to each web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, etc.). If you entered data using Microsoft Edge but the `start` command opened the server on Google Chrome, Chrome will not see Edge's local database.

**How to recover your data:**
1. Open the browser you originally used to enter your data.
2. Navigate to: [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000)
3. If it's the correct browser, all your data will be present!
